paper_metadata.title: Harnessing Bayesian Statistics to Accelerate Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation

summary: The paper introduces Bayesian Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation (BIQAE), showing via simulations that it reduces quantum sample complexity by about 12–15% compared with IQAE‑CP and maintains the expected O(1/ε log log(1/ε)) scaling versus classical Monte Carlo’s O(1/ε²). In molecular benchmarks (H2, LiH, HF, BeH2), BIQAE reduces oracle calls by 8–13% relative to IQAE‑CP and by 2–3 orders of magnitude compared with Classical QAE at ε≈10⁻³, though all results are obtained in noiseless simulation.

experiments.description: Iterative quantum amplitude estimation benchmark on arbitrary quantum amplitudes using Beta-BIQAE, compared against Classical QAE, IQAE-CP/CH, BAE, MLQAE, FQAE, and QAES via numerical simulation.

algorithm.variant: Beta-BIQAE (Bayesian Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation with beta prior); includes IQAE-CP/IQAE-CH as noninformative-prior baselines
algorithm.convergence_criteria: stop when the confidence/credible interval radius for the amplitude reaches target accuracy ε

hyperparameters.K_schedule: adaptive IQAE schedule; benchmarked against base-3 hybrid schedule in theory
target_accuracies: multiple target accuracies over several orders of magnitude; figures include ε from 10^-2 to 10^-8
hyperparameters.sample_batching: incremental batches of Nincre shots per iteration

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Prior initialized from previous stage posterior; for benchmark simulations, amplitude a set to 0.5 in scaling experiments

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Single ancilla amplitude-estimation oracle A prepares state with target amplitude a; Grover amplification uses Q = AS0A†Sψ0
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate quantum amplitude a in A|0...0> = sqrt(1-a)|ψ0>|0> + sqrt(a)|ψ1>|1>
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Iterative quadrant-index tracking; Bayesian credible intervals replace frequentist confidence intervals in BIQAE

problem_instance.description: Synthetic amplitude-estimation benchmark for arbitrary quantum amplitudes; main scaling plots use a=0.5

dataset_specification.description: Mock Q-operator circuit used for classical simulation of amplitude amplification

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 200 repetitions for main scaling comparisons; additional 1000-repetition analyses in appendix figures; compare quantum sample complexity across target accuracies and amplitudes

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical post-processing includes Bayesian updating, credible-interval computation, and stage-to-stage prior preparation; molecular benchmarks use VQE-prepared states and Qiskit Nature/PySCF preprocessing
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute credible intervals, infer next K via linear search, transform posterior to prior for next stage

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper emphasizes that the improvement is in oracle/sample complexity and that constant factors depend on the prior and schedule.

speedup_claims.conditions: benchmark amplitude a = 0.5 over six orders of magnitude in target accuracy; 200 repetitions
speedup_claims.caveats: Observed improvement is near-constant across target accuracies; exact percentage varies with accuracy and amplitude.

speedup_claims.conditions: Normal-BIQAE stage-wise upper bound under normal approximation
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a stage-wise bound for the normal-prior implementation, not the beta-prior implementation used in the main empirical results.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: BIQAE / IQAE: O((1/ε) log log(1/ε)) up to constants; Classical QAE: O(1/ε^2); AAE under small-angle assumption: O(1/√ε) in the special a=O(ε) regime
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: For amplitude estimation baseline, O(1/ε^2) oracle calls
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: Lower constant factor for Beta-BIQAE than IQAE-CP/CH and BAE; exact constant not fully specified except theoretical bounds

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not reported; complexity analysis only gives asymptotic scaling
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Fault‑tolerant quantum computer capable of executing amplitude estimation circuits with large Grover operator counts and precise sampling; logical qubits and deep coherent circuits required
limiting_factors: Experiments performed only via classical simulation
